utterances.text: Did you, yourself, ever wear a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Police? No, I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My question was whether you ever wore a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you wear a variety of different kinds of military uniforms or only one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Initially as I said we were all civilians. People wore their own clothes. When we were issued uniforms, there were camouflage, and this is what I wore until the 30th November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you recall the date on which you were issued your uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Maybe at the beginning of June to us, the regular army, not before the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I request that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: MLD 24, how often would you say you saw Milan Lukic in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: In June 1992, I would see him only when I would go to town from the front line. I would see him with a Commander Tomic. He was driving that car around, and this is the only circumstances of me seeing him then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you see him in a VRS uniform or a police uniform; or sometimes one, sometimes the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No. They didn't change their uniforms. They -- the police had one type of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So which uniform did you see Milan Lukic wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: In the camouflage police uniform. They had slightly different equipment and gear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say "slightly different equipment and gear," what are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Different from ours. Different colour patterns, different colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you see Milan Lukic with a sniper rifle or an automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him with a sniper rifle. Throughout the war, but he did have an automatic rifle, all the troops had automatic rifles. I -- about a sniper rifle, I don't believe that there was a single one in my company. I don't even maybe know how to recognise one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So if you don't know how to recognise one, you can't be sure whether you saw Milan Lukic carrying one or not. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him with such a rifle. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You saw Milan Lukic wearing a variety of different insignias. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that either. I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So which insignia did you see him wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Well, eagle emblem all the troops, all the military personnel wore such eagles.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall the precise dates in June of 1992 when you saw Milan Lukic in a camouflage uniform with an eagle insignia?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, overly broad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It is it actually a price question about the price dates, it couldn't be more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall the dates in June or any other month. I cannot tell you the precise dates. I'm sure I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you cannot recall whether or not you saw him in June of 1992 on any particular day. Is that your evidence? You cannot recall whether you saw Milan Lukic or not on any particular day, in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I used to see him in June 1992, but I could not recall the proper dates. I really wasn't mindful of the dates at the time, but did I see him during June.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So how many times would you estimate you saw Milan Lukic in Visegrad in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Whenever I would have a day off from the front line, I would go to Visegrad and every time I would see him in the car driving around. I cannot specify how many times that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you give a precise date as to when you saw Milan Lukic with Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I just told you whenever I saw him I would see him with Tomic throughout June and until the end of July, I would use -- used to see him with Tomic and Zjelko, until he was killed. He was killed in June. And the other were killed on the 19th of July. I know that because I attended Tomic's funeral.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you testified that whenever you would have day off from the front line, you would go to Visegrad and every time you would see him in the car driving around. How many times would you say --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. He would drive the car, but the commander would be sitting in the passenger seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So approximately how many times would you say in June of 1992 you would have had a day off and gone into Visegrad and seen Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Well, you know, we had seven-day stints, maybe ten-day stints, sometimes 15-day stints, depending on the number of available troops, which means that at least three to four times I went home for rest and recreation during month of June 1992, that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you're planning on taking a break, this might be a pausing point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we do that, just before it goes of the screen, page 71, lines 14 through 17, they are going to need to be listened to because there was evidence as to the dates of death and the funeral, and that's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what is the point, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll need to have the audio record listened to lines 14 to 17 because he testified as to the funeral and the dates of the death for the individuals and that's not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a procedure for this. We use it on an normal daily basis. Our case manager is happy to provide them with a form that they can use to submit for transcript corrections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we will use the normal procedure, not court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, it would -- since -- since when does it become the defendant's responsibility to maintain a transcript in this purest sense of the word. I mean, I think the problem is, is from a staffing perspective every time we fill out a form, it is time taken away from some other pertinent bit of business within the office. That one of the issues, and the thing is, is some of -- the only way we can make the record properly reflective is here in court as it is happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've filled this form many times. It takes less than three minutes, and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And they rotate an attorney for -- by witnesses by several days, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying that you're over-resourced, and what -- Mr. Alarid will find the time to do it. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: MLD 24, can you hear me? Sir, can you hear me clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I know it's been a long day, I appreciate your cooperation. Sir, earlier on you mentioned somebody named Dragan Lukic. Can you confirm for us whether that person still alive today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, he sure is alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And was he referred to, or is he referred to as Drago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No. Just Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now earlier on you mentioned the Holy Trinity celebration, which is a -- a special Serb Orthodox holiday lasting three days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes. The first Holy Trinity, the second day of Holy Trinity, and the third day of Holy Trinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you also testified that you would have some days when you would go in town. Were you able to take off the Holy Trinity holidays from your operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No. It was coincidental that I went back home to take a bath, but I returned the next day. I came home on the 13th of June, I have always maintained that and returned on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And so which of those days was Holy Trinity -- which one of those days was one of the days of Holy Trinity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now how much would you say saw you Sredoje Lukic in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This witness never mentioned that he saw Sredoje Lukic in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you have occasion, Ms. Marcus, to refer to Sredoje before?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I referred to Sredoje before in terms of whether -- we are in closed session; is that right? We're not. It was referred to before in terms of knowledge of the family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'll add a question as to whether or not he saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Due to my best recollection, the name of my client was just mentioned in relation. Was he a family member or not, nothing more than that. And I can give the reference. That was on the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we have been through this before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As part of her indication.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just pose a question about whether or not he saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, I'll take one step back in my questioning. Did you see Sredoje Lukic in Visegrad in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. He was a professional policeman, an active policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So how often, approximately, would you say you saw him in Visegrad in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Two, three times, not more. When I went to town it was rare that I would see him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now just it clarify your last statement, if I understood it, you said, "whenever I went to town it was rare that I would see him as well."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, less often.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Less often than you would see Milan Lukic. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now when you saw Sredoje Lukic did you see him with a weapon; and, if so, what kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: His were the same weapons with this -- difference that he was an active professional policeman. I would sometimes see him in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So presumably he wore the same insignias as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yeah, policemen's insignia. Yes, genuine policemen's insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe the policemen's insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: They were -- they -- the uniform was camouflage but blue, and they wore -- wore the -- policeman's caps.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now specifically about the insignia -- is it the same?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise. If it is possible to hear the best translation for the type of policeman's caps. Even if we can have in the brackets the term which witness mentioned, "sapka."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Interpreters can we have that? "Sapka." Interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is an "sapka," a policemen's cap with a visor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you just said that Sredoje Lukic would have been wearing a policemen's insignia, a genuine policemen's insignia. Can you describe that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I knew that they had insignia on the sleeves. It was a policemen's insignia, like any other policemen, they wore them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you be -- is there any detail about the insignia that you can tell us about, that you can describe, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I can't remember any details. I wasn't really looking carefully. I didn't have anything to do with the police. I didn't cooperate with them, I would just pass them by on my way to work and back.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer to call up ERN Y0268884. If that helps, that is also 65 ter -- on Milan Lukic, 65 ter number 21. I have another number. 1D22-0079.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the document on the left side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I can't see very well, and I can't recognise it. I just see my signature at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. So can you confirm that this is the statement that you gave to the Defence of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, in this statement, if I could request, please, that we have also have the English. In the middle of the statement it says: "The" -- "The Beli Orlovi," which was the White Eagles, "wore camouflage, were armed with automatic rifles, and wore red berets with eagle insignias." Can you describe this sign of the eagle in bit more detail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: We call it the White Eagle patch on the cap. I never had one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So if you saw the sign of the eagle, then you would have assumed that that person was a member of the White Eagles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Not necessarily. There were other troops who had the eagle sign on their caps, the active duty personnel in the army and others.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we ask that this statement be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P25 -- Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I guess it should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I now request ERN 0646-1660.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, this is the eagle insignia which you just described in your statement and now in your testimony. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must say, that was a timed objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No described a patch, Your Honour. He describe a patch, a White Eagle patch. This is it not a patch.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The word used was "insignia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see patch, and on the transcript, it says patch.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, you just confirmed, haven't you, that this, what you see in front you, is a symbol that you would have assumed to be a member of the White Eagles. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I didn't see that before. I just knew that the eagle was on the cap, on the forehead. I never saw any on the sleeve.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. So if this were to be a cap, if this is a symbol on a cap then this would be, to your knowledge, could be the symbol of the White Eagles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, again, misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She is asking him a question. She can't ask him a question, whether this is the symbol of the White Eagles. Seems like a perfectly ordinary question. What is the answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to answer the question? Would you like me to repeat it? Let me repeat the question. I'm sorry to ask you so many times, the same thing. If you were to see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you didn't ask me -- I don't know if you're asking me or someone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, Mr. MLD 24. So now I will ask you the question just one more time. If you were to see this symbol that you see on the screen in front of you, would it have been reasonable for you to assume that this was a White Eagle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I can't know. Lots of people had that sign on their caps, and we had it. The White Eagle was also worn on the red berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you testified earlier that you met Milan Lukic's parents in Rujiste on the 13th of June, and that they --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that they were crying and they told you they feared that Milan may be dead. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Around 4.00 p.m., when I set off on my way home.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What specifically did Milan Lukic's parents tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: They told me I was going by them. They were crying, and they -- I asked them, mile, why are you crying? And he said at Sjemec-Kopita up there, there was some sort of fighting, some troops had fallen, I think Milan might have been among them. I said don't worry. Why don't you call up his commander Slavko Vojnovic and find out, and then I went home. As soon as I got home my wife told me some soldiers had gotten killed. I heard one of them was Zlatko Drivkovic [phoen], Novica Savic, and Veljko Mirkovic; those were the three who were killed. I don't know what time it was, but I know as soon as I got home my wife told me that much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So what you just said was that they told you that they think Milan might have been among them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: That's what they were afraid of. They were afraid he -- he might have been among those killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, did they tell you how they knew, how they -- what caused them to have this fear? Did they tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I didn't ask them how they found out about the incident. I just told them not cry until they found out exactly what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have any communication devices in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Not at the village, no. There was -- there were no communication devices at the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, you were guarding Rujiste on that day, were you? Were you among the guards at Rujiste on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Not that day. I said that we stood guard before, from the 10th until the 19th April. That's when the village guards were on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So who was guarding Rujiste on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: You mean on the 13th of June and around that day? They were still people remaining in the village, men remaining in the village who had not gone to the front line, and they guarded the village, but I was not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, how many men would you say were guarding Rujiste village on the 13th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Well, I could tell you about all the village. Just -- Gojko Jovanovic, Momcilo Nikolic, Radomir Gavrilovic, Vidoje Pejovic, and Drago Jovanovic. Those men were in the village still.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So I think you listed five. Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Well, I told you exactly which men were in the village at that time. You count them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now a number of those men from -- who were guarding Rujiste were actually rounded up and sent on an operation in Kopito. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Well, there were usually around 20 men on the forward line. Where I was there were 22 or 23, and perhaps some more in other places. Not more than 50 men in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could just intervene for the transcript, lines - I just lost it - 18 through 21 there is going to need to be redactions of his village's name if we are in open session, which I believe we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, were you in Rujiste village on the morning of the 13th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I arrived in the evening of the 13th of June to my home, in fact around 4.00. That morning I set off towards my home in a van.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you left Rujiste village in the morning to set off to your home, which we're not going name because we're in public session, in the morning of the 13th. Is that right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: 4.00 p.m. It was the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to need to clarify. Again, I'm sorry to focus on the details. You testified that you met Milan Lukic's parents in Rujiste village on the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes. Because their tent was there. All the civilians were sleeping in tents close to our tent. I said that at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Right. Now my question was whether you were in Rujiste village on the morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, I was, all the way until 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you were no doubt there when a group of the guards at Rujiste were rounded up and deployed on the operation in Kopito. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I don't know who was rounded up. I never heard anything about that. Maybe from another platoon or from another unit, not from my platoon, certainly. Nobody was rounded up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned some names of some persons whom you heard from your wife had been killed on that day. Can you repeat the names, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Vlatko Trifkovic, commander of the battalion; Novica Savic; and Veljko Mirkovic. Those three men had gotten killed at Lijeska.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to read a few lines of what you testified to earlier. I'm reading from what is now page 42, line 10. You said: "When I came home my wife said," and then your name is there, "three men died in Gornje Lesce," which I suppose would be Lijeska, "commander who was the battalion commander who got killed. Vlatko Filipovic, and another man, Veljko, got killed. I don't know if they had any connections, but eventually I found out that he wasn't killed." So am I right to understand this as saying you don't know if Milan Lukic had any connections with those commanders who were killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had any connection, I'm not insure. All I know that he was up there on those days, the 13th, the 14th and the 15th, they were cut off. I heard that over the communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now I just recall you testifying that there were no communications, so maybe I misunderstood your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Redactions from page 83, line 25, through page 84, line 8, the name of the village that needs to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you -- you heard from people in Rujiste about the deployment in Kopita, is that correct, you heard that when you visited there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I did not say that, that they were sent. None of the men from my platoon. I don't know about other platoons. I couldn't have said that. Maybe you misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You heard from Milan Lukic's parents that they thought he might have been deployed to Kopito. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: They knew he was sent to Kopito. I don't know how they found out and they told me so, and that's for sure how it was. There is no mistake about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And is this the only way that you came to believe that Milan Lukic was in Kopito on those dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: He was there for sure, because he didn't come back for three days. The road was opened only on the 15th. You could hear from that the troops. You can hear everything through military communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, what counsel was asking you, you haven't really answered. She asked whether that was the only way that you knew or that you came to believe that Milan Lukic was in Kopito on those dates. That is what you heard from his parents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just from what I heard from his parents and when I came back home, again, I repeat, my wife told me that three men had gotten killed there. She didn't know -- she -- she gave me some names, and the first I heard from it was from Mile and Kata.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was there something particularly remarkable or unusual to make that conversation stick out so clearly in your memory, that conversation you had in Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Just what I told you, and I have a pretty good memory as to what I hear, and I don't tend to forget such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But you unfortunately were not able to tell us the dates on which you saw Milan Lukic in Visegrad in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Because I wasn't interested enough. I didn't keep track. I didn't keep track of the dates. Whenever I went home on leave, I would also go to town. But which dates, those were in June. I didn't remember because I didn't think I would need it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you some about some individuals to see whether you know them. You do know Mitar Vasiljevic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And how do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I know him because he worked as a waiter, and whenever I went to the bar he was there working different shifts. He worked different jobs in several coffee bars and taverns, and he liked his drink, and he was more or less tipsy all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was Mitar Vasiljevic a member of Milan Lukic's group in Visegrad in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, assumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. You have to establish that Milan Lukic did have a group.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, do you confirm that Milan Lukic had a group in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I didn't know -- in fact Milan Lukic did have a group, but Mitar Vasiljevic was not there. He just swept streets. In fact he was in charge of streets sweeping. He would take some people, either Serbs or Muslims and chart them with street sweeping.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know somebody named Radomir Simsic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Radomir Simsic? He is from Glavici village, but he has been living somewhere in Serbia close to Belgrade for a long time. He was in the initial boot camp training with me in the army. I know the man, but he had long left for Serbia, somewhere close to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge of Radomir Simsic being a member of Milan Lukic's group in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Certainly not. He wasn't even in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know someone named Dusko Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I heard of him. He is also somewhere in Serbia. He had left when I was in Loznica. He used to work in Greben, and then he left for Serbia. I heard of him, but I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know what relation he is, if any to Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Well, they are both Vasiljevics. Same village. I don't know if they are related.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know, to your knowledge, was Dusko Vasiljevic a member of Milan Lukic's group in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I don't know that either. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What about Ljubisa Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I don't know about him either.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You don't know who he is, or you don't know if he was a member of Milan Lukic's group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I heard that Ljubisa and Dusko were brothers, that they lived in Serbia. I don't know whether they were in any way connected with Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: MLD 24, I have just one more name on this list to ask you about and that is a man named Zoran Mitrasinovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I know the man.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: He is from the village of Rijeka, and I know that he worked at the Unis company in Zica. I know him, he is a younger fellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you know him to have operated with Milan Lukic's group in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. He may have, but I'm really not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, since you know him, let me ask you about an another Mitrasinovic. That would be Miodrag Mitrasinovic. Are you familiar with a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Oh, that would probably have been the guy we called Mijo, I know Mijo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you know Mijo to have operated as part of Milan Lukic's group in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I never saw them together. I saw at the outset that I only say Milan and the other people who were who escorted Tomic. They went to various places, but I can't really speak about things I haven't seen and things I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: But only until 10.30 on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you dressed in a military or -- in a military uniform on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Because I was waiting for the van to pick me up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you were carrying an automatic weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, I did, most certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How many times in the days preceding the 14th of June, did you have occasion to visit Koritnik, if at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It is part of the case. I think explaining the relevance will be harmful to the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In other words, if I were to say it, I would be testifying. We'll see how it develops and perhaps Mr. Alarid can wait a few lines and see where this goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you again. How many times in the days preceding the 14th of June of 1992 did you have occasion to visit (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: In June I didn't go to Koritnik at all. Only on the 6th of May I was there to attend a festivity, and I didn't go there again until August because I had didn't have an opportunity to go there, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now there are a few other names I would like to ask you about, in relation to this time-period that we're talking about. Dusan Gavrilovic. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Dusan Gavrilovic. I knew one, but he died. He -- there was a guy by the name of Dusan Grujic, so maybe it is your mistake. But Dusan Gavrilovic died before the war. But the other guy -- and he lived at the entrance to the town, in a quarter called Kalate, but there was a Dusan Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Okay, we can return to open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now this person you've just mentioned Dusan Grujic. Can you tell us, if you know where he was on the 14th of June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: He was at home, and you didn't ask me so far, and with him -- it was with him that the group from Koritnik came to my house, and he lived some 30 metres away from me. And he said, my mother is sick. I have to go home, and he left -- he returned home. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you confirm that Dusan Grujic visited Koritnik and walked with the neighbours from Koritnik to your village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I think we will need a redaction of the mention of the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell who else was with Dusan Grujic that you know of who moved on Koritnik and walked with the neighbours from Koritnik to your village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Nobody but him. And the group of Muslims from Koritnik. Nobody else, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What about somebody named Radomir Djuric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: There is such a person. He is from the village of Loznica. That's further away than Koritnik. It is it towards the Serbian border.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of Radomir Djuric having visited Koritnik in the days before the 14th of June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What about somebody named Dragomir Djuric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: There is no such man.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And a man named Ilija Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I know him. He is a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of him visiting the village of Koritnik in the days prior to 14th of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I don't understand that because he was in town for sure as a police officer. And I don't know that he went to Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What about Radomir Grujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: There is no such person. There -- Djuric, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My apologies for interrupting, just page 94, line 16 and 17, witness said reserve police officer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, I just wanted to request that these kinds of translations, unless they require redactions, could be submitted afterwards, just not to interrupt the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In relation to the words of my learned friend Ms. Marcus, we have a huge problems with the transcript. We request this, just for example, for this Honourable Trial Chamber, two months ago we requested the redaction of some portion of transcript, and we suggested to be use audiotape and videotape from the trial, and we've been still waiting. So that is the reason why we always complain about the transcript problems. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That one was simple. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, on the day that your neighbours from Koritnik came to your village, were you the only person in uniform an armed in your village at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: There was only me. Everybody else was in civilian clothes. And the people I mentioned before were guarding the village, and the younger men were deployed out there in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So all tolled, approximately how many armed men were there in your village on the day that your neighbours from Koritnik passed through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: On that day, there was nobody in my village that was armed because all the able-bodied men were deployed in the field. And the older men were guarding the village. They may have had hunting rifles or something, but there were no armed -- armed men in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And your neighbours who came from Koritnik, none of them bore any weapons nor were any of them wearing any uniforms. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: The people from Koritnik that came to my house were all civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Who was it to your knowledge that suggested to that group that they leave Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who told them nor why they left, only when they came up to my house, they said that they wanted to wait for the bus to take them to it Kladanj. But I don't know who told them to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So these were people whom you had known for a very long, your close neighbours, as you said had you good relationships with them, and yet when you saw them in a very large group come from your village to your village, you didn't ask them, What happened, why -- why did you leave your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: I didn't ask them because they said that they were leaving and they were asking me to come with them to Sase, but I didn't ask them why.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you do not know who it was that told the group from Koritnik to leave Koritnik? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, you testified, I believe, that they expected to meet some buses in Sase. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: They were not under the impression that there would be buses for them in your village, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: They weren't, no, only at Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So, in other words, when they came to your village and they met you in your village, your evidence is that none of them asked you, Where are the buses here? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: They -- they told me that the bus was waiting for me at Sase, and that's why they asked me to come with them. I've said as much several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, I think earlier you said that Radomir -- oh, no, it was Dusan Grujic, I believe, that you said -- please give me one moment. Yes, Dusan Grujic, you said, who accompanied them from Koritnik to your village. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: Yes, up to my house. All the way. And I said a short while ago if you can go with him. I can't because I have to return my mother is on her deathbed, and he immediately went back home.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did he provide you with any information which would explain why these people had left their village?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That specific question was not asked and answered. I asked him whether the people, whether the villagers had told him. I didn't ask him whether this guy had told him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's have the answer, and then we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sir, when Dusan Grujic came escorting your neighbours to your village, did he tell you why they had left their village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD24
utterances.text: No, he didn't. I repeat once more, he did not. And I'm sure he didn't know himself. And they told me that a bus was waiting for them to tame them to Kladanj. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn now until tomorrow morning.
